Subject: ISV Sandbox handoff: instrumentation & tracing acceptance criteria

Hi Ellis / Anya,

Thanks again for the productive session yesterday. As discussed, we're ready to hand over the sandbox with the tracing/instrumentation hooks so your engineering team can run the end-to-end performance and correctness checks. To keep things light and actionable, here's what we need to confirm from your side before we open the sandbox:

- Validation scope: tracing spans + request/response sampling, prefix KV cache behavior, and latency SLO tests at 95th percentile.
- Data controls: confirm you’ll use the sandbox service account (no customer PII) and the provided KMS key for secrets.
- Access window: initial access for 10 business days starting Monday, Aug 9; we can extend if needed.
- Acceptance criteria: successful execution of the included instrumentation checklist (attached), and no regressions in the prompt-suite for the three pilot flows (search, summarization, Q&A).

Attached: isv-instrumentation-checklist.xlsx (xlsx) — quick checklist + test prompts.

Next steps: if that scope looks good, Vanessa will send sandbox credentials and a short runbook. Marissa, can you put a quick mutual action plan (MAP) in HubSpot with milestone dates?

Cheers,

Jordan Blake
Partner PM, ISV Alliances

Subject: Re: ISV Sandbox handoff: instrumentation & tracing acceptance criteria

Jordan — thanks, that plan reads well. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Tracing: we want both span-level timing and a sampled request payload for 1% of requests. Is that OK with the sandbox policy?
2) KV cache: can you include a short test harness that toggles cache TTLs so we can validate cold vs warm behavior?
3) Access: our engineering lead (Anya) will be the primary contact. Could we get read-only logs exported to our S3 for the duration?

We can commit to the 10 business day window and will run the included checklist. We’ll also map the acceptance items to our QA stories and send the results back in a single report.

Thanks — Ellis
